title: Recursive aperture
description: Vermilion and ivory frames fold into a continuous recursive aperture.
useCase: Build an infinite image-space zoom with controllable angular coupling.
reducedMotion: The elapsed-time clock stops. Parameter controls immediately update the static composition.
limitations: Requires WebGL 1; a static CSS swatch appears if unavailable or after context loss. A procedural coordinate-space recursion, not nested DOM or a navigable 3D tunnel.
look: Op-art tunnel of nested square frames with vermilion side and ivory top-and-bottom trapezoids, thick black bands between them, receding to a centre point.
motion: Frames expand outward from the centre in a seamless logarithmic zoom, one 2.7× layer roughly every 9 s; the twist slider rotates each layer in proportion to depth, either direction.
adapt: The `FRAGMENT` shader maps each pixel to log depth (`log(2.7)` per frame, `u_time*.11` speed) and twists with `rot((u_control-.5)*.7*depth)`; `edge` and `bevel` shape the black bands. Recolour `red`, `paper` and `black`; keep the context-loss and reduced-motion handling.
